exposure: Intention to give birth at freestanding midwifery units
Intention to give birth at tertiary-level maternity units
outcome: Admission to neonatal intensive care unit or special care nursery
Management of third stage of labor
cohort: 494 women who intended to give birth at freestanding midwifery units and 3157 women who intended to give birth at tertiary-level maternity units in New South Wales, Australia. Participants had low-risk, singleton pregnancies and were at less than 28(+0) weeks gestation at the time of booking.
finding: Planning to give birth in a freestanding midwifery unit was associated with a higher likelihood of spontaneous vaginal birth and a lower likelihood of cesarean section, with no significant differences in 5-minute Apgar scores but a lower likelihood of neonatal intensive care or special care nursery admission.
mod_finding: Women who planned to give birth at a freestanding midwifery unit were significantly more likely to have a spontaneous vaginal birth and significantly less likely to have a caesarean section.
gest_age: Less than 28 weeks at time of booking
